commentary: A verification of the two proposal walks over the blind pair's 19 findings. Every resolved entry's edit was read at its sites in proposal, design, both delta specs and tasks, then the residual diff from the external return's commit was listed: six files, each inside some entry's edit record, so no record gap. The one regression is the resolver entry's new sentence about which subcommands meet gh-absent; it miscounts by forgetting program, which also queries the default branch. The dangling title is outside the walk record: the walk renamed the ADDED requirement in its own prose but no entry recorded the rename, so no sweep searched the wrapped form. Both are text repairs in one spec file. The carrier narrowing, the message file outside the tree, the push destination and the default-branch reliance on propose's collision check all read consistently across the five artifacts, and orbit validate passes.

verification.title: resolve(run, {withDefault: false}) still requires gh: the 'never needs gh' premise is false against the code
Bodies with no resolvable change target hit orbit pr commit's usage error, not 'off', so G0 fails at the defaults
git add -A stages the body's own <message-file> when it is written inside the work tree, and observations.untracked never names it
The verify row fires the step inside a system review: Pass 0 invokes /orbit:verify in the reviewing session
Explore's step position disagrees: spec says after each boundary emit, design D4 and task 2.2 say at its close
D7's 'a reader of either finds the other' is one-way: the tail's requirement is unchanged and names no step
The step's lines land after the eligibility line, which the No-chaining contract says ends the turn
A proceed with nothing to stage and nothing to push prints one empty segment; the step's 'on proceed it writes the commit message' over-reads it
The merge-in-progress row misses a cherry-pick or revert stopped without conflicts
A push with no upstream never sets one, so the push reprints at every close
The No-chaining sentence restates part of the step's gate
docs/commands.md's per-command text is not in the docs task
Default-branch protection has an undefined fail-open case
Push eligibility compares against a potentially different destination
